description: The AGPC-code research team publishes configurable Python notebooks for training, applying and checking population-mapping models. The documented sequence trains an XGBoost model, creates gridded predictions and calculates validation metrics. Separate year-specific inputs and parameters were used for the 2010 and 2020 baseline models associated with the annual 500 m population dataset for China. GitHub and Zenodo provide the notebooks openly under the MIT licence at no cost. The README recommends Python 3.9 or later and requires identical dimensions, resolution, coordinate reference system, affine transform and grid alignment across predictor rasters. Input data are not bundled and must be obtained separately. The notebooks were not run in this review. They could prepare gridded demand or exposure populations for infrastructure simulations after validating local predictors and constraints. The code complements the published AGPC rasters by exposing a configurable modelling sequence; it does not directly generate all annual estimates from unprepared source data.
